view: Macro is a mild headwind for a long-duration mega-cap (10y 5.0, 30y 5.35, real 10y 2.66, CPI 3.7 rising to a 3.9 forecast against Fed funds 4.0, breadth rotating to equal-weight), offset by benign growth and credit (ISM 55.5, HY OAS 3.3, NFCI -0.46, VIX 17.62). NVDA's -15.45% week is overwhelmingly idiosyncratic: SOX +7.99%, AMD +30.2%, SPX -0.45% the same week, so macro explains little of the move and earnings on 2026-11-17 dominates the 2-week bucket.

probabilities.defs: 2w ±5%, quarters ±10%, vs price_at_call 165.785. next_2_weeks: up = close > 174.07, down = close < 157.50, range between, measured at close 2026-11-26. this_quarter: to last close of 2026-12-31; next_quarter: to last close of 2027-03-31; up > 182.36, down < 149.21, range between. up + range + down = 100.

evidence.point: Outside view 33/45/22 (n=258). I cut range by 5, raise down by 6 and trim up by 1 (to 32/40/28) for the earnings binary (wider tails) and a rate/inflation headwind. Total shift is small because macro is not the driver here.

Base 39/43/18. Took 3 points each off up and range and added 6 to down (to 36/40/24) because the window contains FOMC 2026-12-09 and CPI 2026-12-10 with CPI forecast 3.9 vs prev 3.7, i.e. inflation re-accelerating with yields already at 5.0 (10y).

Base 50/31/19. Trimmed up by 4 and range by 1, added 5 to down (46/30/24): high real yields and megacap-to-equal-weight rotation are a slow-moving drag. Conditional base rates (RSI<=36: 69% up; 2w drop <=-15%: 100% up, n=4) point the other way but are tiny, overlapping samples and outside my lane; treated as weak.
Real 10y 2.66 with nominal 10y 5.0 and 30y 5.35 (TLT 80.22): a restrictive discount-rate backdrop that penalises long-duration equities. Headwind.
CPI YoY 3.7 vs Fed funds 4.0: policy only slightly above inflation, and calendar shows CPI forecast 3.9 for 2026-12-10, limiting room for easing. Headwind into the Dec 9 FOMC.

Curve positively sloped (10y-3m 0.68, 10y-2y 0.25): not an inversion recession signal; bear-steepening flavour consistent with term-premium pressure rather than growth scare. Neutral to mild headwind for duration.
HY OAS 3.3 and NFCI -0.46: credit tight and financial conditions loose. No systemic stress. Tailwind / no headwind.
ISM PMI 55.5, new orders 55.5, 4-wk claims 195250: growth firmly in expansion. Supports capex demand; not a recession regime.

RSP 1m +4.03 vs SPY 1m -2.12 (ratio 0.2921), S5TH 63.81% above 200d: breadth broadening away from cap-weighted megacaps. Healthy market, but a rotation headwind specifically for the largest names like NVDA.
VIX 17.62: no broad risk-off. NVDA's drop is not happening in a macro panic.

NVDA -15.45% week vs SOX +7.99%, SMH +4.83%, AMD +30.2%, AVGO +17.46%, TSM +7.53%, SPX -0.45%, NDX +1.6%. Beta 1.75 times SPX -0.45% implies under 1% of macro-explained move; the rest is stock-specific (share shift within semis). Macro explains very little of this move.
NVDA YTD -12.67% vs SOX +45.29%, SPX +11.14%: underperformance is persistent and sector-relative, not macro.

Dated catalysts: PPI 2026-11-13 (fcst 0.4, prev 1.3); Retail sales + NVDA earnings 2026-11-17; opex 2026-11-20; Core PCE/GDP 2026-11-25; ISM 2026-12-01 (prev 55.5); NFP 2026-12-04 (prev 165K); FOMC 2026-12-09; CPI 2026-12-10 (fcst 3.9). Before the print, macro data matter at the margin; after 2026-11-17 the Dec 9-10 FOMC/CPI pair is the main macro risk for this_quarter.
Options positioning is not available this run (not in slice): unknown, not neutral. Lowers my confidence on the earnings-week tail split.

what_would_change_my_mind: More bullish: CPI on 2026-12-10 prints at or below 3.7 (vs 3.9 forecast) and FOMC 2026-12-09 is dovish, with real 10y falling below 2.66 and 10y below 5.0.
More bullish: RSP/SPY ratio turning down from 0.2921 (rotation back to megacaps).
More bearish: HY OAS widening above 3.3 together with NFCI rising above -0.46 and VIX above 17.62 trending higher (macro risk-off joins the idiosyncratic selling).
More bearish: ISM on 2026-12-01 falling well below 55.5 alongside 30y above 5.35 (stagflation mix).
Earnings 2026-11-17: if NVDA keeps diverging from SOX after the print, my macro read stays near-irrelevant; if NVDA re-couples with SOX, macro beta matters more for the quarter buckets.
notes_for_chair: Macro explains almost none of the week: NVDA -15.45% vs SOX +7.99% and AMD +30.2%. The question is stock-specific (competitive share shift or company news) - for the fundamentals/news members, not macro. Check governance/export news against TB1/TB3.
